values: Free Expense Report Template for Excel + Printable PDF
Blank is for your work. Filled example is fictional. Keep the original file.
Yellow cells are editable; gray cells calculate. Do not overwrite formulas.
Ten rows per form. Extra rows need formula and total-range checks; use another version instead.
Nonnegative numbers, at most two decimals. Quantity accepts three decimals. Invalid or partial rows block final amounts.
One currency code labels all amounts; no conversion. Browser JSON backups do not import into this workbook.
Save as a new .xlsx, reopen it, change one amount, and verify the total before operational use.
Select A1:H33 on the required form tab. Choose landscape, Print Selection, and fit one page. Check all text in print preview.
Built and round-trip tested with Artifact Tool. Native Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets have not been certified. Keep original formulas when converting.
Complete header and manual review fields yourself. Draft totals and typed status do not authorize a transaction.

Employee-paid eligible costs are $120 travel + $40 supplies + $18 parking = $178. A separate $50 company-paid room remains visible in recorded costs, but is excluded from the claim. Subtract the $60 advance and $0 prior reimbursement: $118 remains payable.
Use one claimant, report reference, reporting period and currency. Enter dates as fixed dates so the saved claim keeps the same period.
Enter the date, merchant, business purpose, category and receipt reference. Select Employee or Company for who paid. Keep the supporting documents with your own records.
For employee-paid rows, enter the amount your reviewer considers eligible. It cannot exceed the recorded cost. Company-paid rows must have eligible amount 0. Eligibility is a manual policy decision.
Enter advances and prior reimbursement once. If they exceed eligible costs, the negative net amount stays visible for a return or reconciliation review.
Check evidence and your policy, record the reviewer and status, then save a dated copy. A status entered in this worksheet is a record, not an approval signature or payment.

A receipt reference helps you find a document; this worksheet does not upload or verify it. The IRS recordkeeping guidance describes supporting documents such as receipts and invoices. This form does not decide deductibility, mileage rates or tax treatment.
